records.verificationNote: All ACE inhibitors on the list are Tier 2, MT, with no PA or step therapy flag (p.35). Lisinopril is chosen as the most common agent in the class. Scope p.3: the Essential Formulary applies to the listed Small Group plans (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum) and Individual Marketplace plans (Bronze 07-20, Silver 26-35, Gold 08). Page numbers are PDF page indexes (PDF page 11 = printed page 1). The document has no statement that the list is exhaustive. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: Re-read by x-coordinate column; tier, PA, ST, QL flags confirmed, no change.]

preferredAgent.plainSig: Take one 10 mg tablet by mouth once a day, every day, for blood pressure or heart failure.

records.verificationNote: Read directly from the UnitedHealthcare 2026 PDL, effective January 1, 2026, pages 19-20 (Cardiovascular section covering antihypertensives). Confirmed: 'lisinopril oral 1', 'lisinopril-hydrochlorothiazide 1', 'benazepril hcl oral 1', 'benazepril-hydrochlorothiazide 1' (page 19), 'captopril oral 1' (page 19), 'enalapril maleate oral tablet 1', 'enalapril maleate oral solution 3 PA', 'enalapril-hydrochlorothiazide 1', 'fosinopril sodium 1' (page 20) -- all generic ACE inhibitors are Tier 1 with no PA except the enalapril oral solution liquid formulation, which is Tier 3 PA. No brand-name ACE inhibitor (e.g., Zestril, Prinivil, Vasotec, Lotensin) is separately listed as still marketed/covered -- LOTENSIN and LOTENSIN HCT appear on page 20 at Tier 4 (brand benazepril), confirming brand is non-preferred versus generic. Ramipril was searched for but not found as a distinct line item in the pages read; the class as a whole is generically dominated at Tier 1 per the PDL's generic medication policy (page 5). [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]

records.verificationNote: Read pages 46 to 50: lisinopril 2.5 to 40 mg tablets, Tier 1, no UM. Every ACE inhibitor on the list carries no PA or ST. Combination products (lisinopril-HCTZ, benazepril-HCTZ, enalapril-HCTZ, amlodipine-benazepril) are excluded as single-agent alternatives. Sig is standard label dosing. [Reused: same national Humana Premier Rx PDP formulary as the TX guide (2026-10-21)]
